correctness.rationale: Block multiplication leaves only the upper-right commutator u_i v_j−u_j v_i, with all Z_i free. Equivalently each column of U wedges to zero with each column of V in k^t. If each side has a nonzero column, one from each side spans a common line, and all other columns must be on that line; otherwise U=0 or V=0. This proves the union over every extension, including characteristic two. The rank-at-most-one locus is geometrically irreducible by outer-product parametrization, of dimension t+r+s−1 by its one-dimensional nonzero factorization fibers. In the permitted range both pure loci have rank-two witnesses, and a mixed rank-one witness lies in neither pure locus. Thus all three are maximal; adding rst yields the dimensions. Equality of the first two forces r=s=d, and equality with the third then gives t=2+1/(d−1), so (2,2,3) is the sole equidimensional case, of dimension 18. Over F_q the two pure loci contribute q^(rt)+q^(st)−1 centered-block-free matrices, and each of (q^r−1)(q^s−1)/(q−1) mixed row lines gives q^t−1 matrices. Multiplying by q^(rst) yields the stated all-arity exact count. No scheme assertion was needed for the frozen proof.
residual_risks: Finding concerns labeled tuples, not conjugacy orbits. Its reduced-variety scope and r,s,t≥2 restrictions are material to the stated component count.

evidence: Rauh indexes prime components by retained subsets Y such that each omitted vertex connects at least two components of the induced graph on Y when restored.

For K_{r,s}, any proper Y meeting both sides is connected and fails this condition. A one-sided Y cannot omit a vertex of that same side because it has no neighbors in Y. Thus Y is exactly the full vertex set or one whole side; r,s≥2 makes each whole-side set admissible.
Goodwin–Röhrle independently covers only the (1,1,m) pair boundary.
broader_coverage.reasoning: For full Y Rauh's equations impose overall rank at most one. For one whole side, each retained vertex is an isolated singleton, so there are no new minors within that side and all other columns vanish. These are exactly the frozen three components.

originality.rationale: The commuting equations are exactly a generalized binomial edge ideal for the complete bipartite graph K_{r,s}, with independent central variables adjoined. Rauh's 2012 preprint/2013 paper, Section 3 Lemma 5 and Theorem 7, gives a general primary decomposition that yields the exact three component ideals here, not merely a related rank argument. The dimensions, integer equidimensionality test and finite-field census are immediate calculations in this explicit decomposition, not independent substantive additions.
residual_risks: No independent publication of the exact count was identified; the count's status as a direct corollary is established mathematically, not inferred from a search miss.

value.rationale: The Lie interpretation is instructive, but the known graph-ideal decomposition determines every component immediately. The only residual calculations are equality of three known dimensions and a disjoint count of two affine spaces plus mixed rank-one matrices. The record does not establish any further geometric or arithmetic phenomenon that survives this coverage as an independently valuable contribution, and adjoining a scheme-reducedness claim would also be covered.
residual_risks: This judgment concerns novelty-bearing value of the submitted specialization, not the usefulness of the general graph-ideal theorem or of expository applications.
